question: Which anatomical structure is part of the external female genitalia known as the vulva?
explanation: The labia majora form the outer protective folds of the external female genitalia, whereas the other structures are located within the internal reproductive tract. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T8#GNS216_U5_T8_h1)

question: Why does cancer spread quickly to the lymph nodes in vulval tumours?

options.A: Infections are rare in the perineal region
options.B: The vulva has a rich network of lymphatic vessels
options.C: Tumour cells multiply slowly in pelvic tissue

explanation: A rich lymphatic drainage system in the vulval region provides direct pathways for cancer cells to reach regional lymph nodes early. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T8#GNS216_U5_T8_h1)

question: What is the most common type of malignant vulval tumour?
explanation: Squamous cell carcinoma makes up the vast majority of all diagnosed malignant vulval growths. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T8#GNS216_U5_T8_h2)

question: Which of the following is a non-cancerous (benign) vulval growth?
explanation: Bartholin gland cysts are non-cancerous fluid-filled swellings, unlike carcinomas and sarcomas which are malignant. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T8#GNS216_U5_T8_h2)

question: Which chronic skin condition is strongly linked to non-HPV-related vulval cancer?
explanation: Long-standing lichen sclerosus causes chronic irritation and skin changes that increase the risk of cancer over time. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T8#GNS216_U5_T8_h3)

question: How does tobacco smoking contribute to the development of vulval tumours?

options.A: It prevents the clearance of normal bacterial flora
options.B: It causes immediate hypertrophy of Bartholin glands
options.C: It suppresses local immune surveillance in mucosal tissues
options.D: It directly alters the pH of vaginal secretions

explanation: Smoking introduces carcinogens and impairs local immune responses, making it harder for the body to clear cellular abnormalities. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T8#GNS216_U5_T8_h3)

question: What is the most common early symptom reported by patients with a vulval tumour?
explanation: Chronic, unremitting itching is typically the earliest and most frequent complaint that brings a patient to the clinic. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T8#GNS216_U5_T8_h4)

question: A patient presents with a non-healing sore on the labia majora that bleeds easily. What should the nurse suspect?

options.D: A potential malignant vulval lesion requiring investigation

explanation: Non-healing ulcers and bleeding masses on the vulva are classic clinical signs of malignancy that must be biopsied. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T8#GNS216_U5_T8_h4)

question: Which test gives a definitive diagnosis of vulval cancer?
explanation: Examining a tissue sample under a microscope via a biopsy is the only definitive way to confirm cancer. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T8#GNS216_U5_T8_h5)

question: Why is a pelvic MRI or CT scan ordered after a vulval biopsy confirms cancer?

options.A: To evaluate the depth of invasion and lymph node status
options.B: To screen for concurrent gastrointestinal infections
options.C: To measure baseline hormone levels in the blood
options.D: To determine the patient's blood group and genotype

explanation: Imaging staging tests help determine how far the tumour has spread into surrounding tissues and nearby lymph nodes. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T8#GNS216_U5_T8_h5)

question: What is the primary treatment modality for most localized malignant vulval tumours?
explanation: Surgery is the mainstay of treatment for localized vulval cancer to remove the primary lesion and assess regional nodes. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T8#GNS216_U5_T8_h6)

question: When is radiation therapy often combined with chemotherapy for vulval cancer?

options.A: To shrink advanced tumours before surgery or treat unresectable cases
options.B: To prevent the initial onset of lichen sclerosus
options.C: To replace the need for any subsequent physical examinations
options.D: To cure benign cysts without the need for drainage

explanation: Chemoradiation is valuable for reducing tumour bulk prior to surgery or managing patients who are poor surgical candidates. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T8#GNS216_U5_T8_h6)

question: Which complication must nurses monitor for following radical vulvectomy and lymph node dissection?
explanation: Removal of inguinal and femoral lymph nodes disrupts fluid drainage from the legs, putting patients at risk for lymphoedema. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T8#GNS216_U5_T8_h7)

question: What is an important component of holistic nursing care for a patient undergoing vulval surgery?

options.A: Addressing body image concerns and sexual health impacts
options.B: Insisting that family members make all medical decisions
options.C: Restricting all physical movement for six weeks

explanation: Surgeries involving the external genitalia carry significant psychological and sexual consequences that require compassionate nursing support. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T8#GNS216_U5_T8_h7)
